messages:
Maya C (support): FYI - ACME (ticket CS-2147) reported what looks like raw prompt data in our audit logs. They say the payload contains possible customer PII. Can security confirm scope and advise on customer notification timeline? They are on Hosted API, org: acme-inc, sample request_id: req_8f3b9c.

Kevin L (oncall): Thanks Maya. Can you paste the exact log snippet and the API trace id? I can pull storage access logs and check bucket paths.

Maya C (support): Pasted snippet they sent (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T15:10:12Z req_8f3b9c model=redwood-v1 prompt="John Doe, SSN: 123-45-6789, order details..."
storage_path: gs://redwood-audit/hosted/acme-inc/2026/03/17/log-req_8f3b9c.json
```
They said this came from our audit log export pipeline. Ticket includes customer account created 2024-11-02.

Raj P (security): Ok — initial triage: we need to know if this is an isolated ingestion (single request) or wider. Kevin, please check access logs for that storage_path and list any service account reads/writes between 03/17 00:00Z and 03/18 00:00Z. Also confirm whether those objects are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) or platform keys.

Kevin L (oncall): Running queries now. Quick note: hosted audit exports are normally encrypted with our platform KMS (projects/redwood-audit-key) unless customer opted into KMS-HSM. I'll report back with access list.

Sara T (acct): @Maya how did ACME discover this? Are they asking for remediation + notification now? We need to prep comms and billing impacts if we need to offer credits.

Maya C (support): They flagged during an internal review after pulling logs for debugging. They are asking: 1) scope (what other customers affected) 2) timeline for us to notify if PII exposed 3) whether we can purge/redact those logs immediately.

Anna R (legal): If PII was exposed and it's a breach under governing law, many regs expect notification within a short window (72 hours under GDPR for the supervisory authority; customer notification depends). We need classification from security ASAP. Collect: data types, number of affected users, retention policy applied, and evidence of exfil. Legal recommends we treat as incident until sign-off.

Raj P (security): Preliminary from quick look: object exists at path above and was written by export service at 15:10Z. No signs of external read from that object in the last 90 days (access logs show service-account and internal-process reads). That suggests not egressed externally so far. However, we must confirm processing pipeline before export — did any intermediate logs carry full prompt? Check inference worker debug-level logging around req_8f3b9c.

Kevin L (oncall): Found worker logs for node: worker-17 that show debug dump for the same request. I'm pulling offsets. Also verifying whether debug logging level was enabled for that customer; we disabled debug-level dumps for hosted by default but there's an occasional flag flip.

Maya C (support): ACME claims they didn't enable any flags. They want immediate purge of that object and assurance this won't persist.

Raj P (security): Do NOT delete yet. Forensics: preserve a copy and snapshot storage ACLs. We can take an immutable snapshot and then schedule redaction. I'll coordinate with infra to snapshot and stage a redacted copy. If we purge prematurely we lose evidence needed for scope + legal.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-45 — Security: potential PII in audit exports (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-45) :rotating_light:

Sara T (acct): For customer comms: propose we tell ACME within 24 hours that we're investigating, confirm containment steps, and provide ETA for scope (48 hours) and remediation plan. Legal sign-off required for wording.

Anna R (legal): Agreed. Draft message should be cautious: honest about investigation, avoid definitive 'breach' until security confirms. Prepare a timeline and offer contact for escalation. I'll join live sync if needed.

Raj P (security): Action items assigned:
- Kevin: produce list of accesses and worker debug logs for req_8f3b9c (due in 2 hours).
- Infra: snapshot the object and set retention to prevent deletion (immediate).
- Support (Maya): tell ACME we are investigating and will follow up in 24 hours. (I'll provide a scoped statement)
- Legal (Anna): prepare notification draft template.

Kevin L (oncall): Copy of access query: ```gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_storage_bucket AND protoPayload.resourceName:\"projects/_/buckets/redwood-audit/objects/hosted/acme-inc/2026/03/17/log-req_8f3b9c.json\"" --limit 50```
I'll attach the output to the incident.

Maya C (support): Noted. I'll send a short: "we have initiated an investigation; containment and forensics in progress; will update within 24 hours" message now.

Raj P (security): Status update (30m): no external reads found; worker debug logs indicate the prompt was emitted to audit exporter due to a transient debug flag enabled on a single node. Looks isolated to req_8f3b9c. Still validating retention policy for exported objects older than 90 days.

Anna R (legal): Based on current info, treat as PII exposure incident. Prepare notification options: (A) notify supervisory authority within 72 hours (if applicable) and affected customers within 72 hours; (B) alternative timeline if non-EU data. We need final scope before choosing.

Sara T (acct): I'll prepare customer comms drafts for both options and coordinate on credits/offers.

Maya C (support): Thanks team. I'll paste ACME reply here after I send the 24hr update.

Raj P (security): Final note: after snapshot, infra can redact the stored object and replace with sanitized copy (remove prompt text). We'll document chain-of-custody. Do not perform key rotations or mass deletions until legal approves — those actions can complicate forensics and KMS logs.

Kevin L (oncall): I'll upload the access log export and worker logs to the incident page in 45m.

Maya C (support): ACME replied: "appreciate the quick response. Please confirm when data is redacted and any actions we should take." I'll keep channel posted. :white_check_mark:
